clue.text: Right to divide up cocoa in unusually abundant supply

indicators.note: to divide means this letter splits the other letters apart, sitting inside them
unusually signals that the letters of up, cocoa and in are arranged in an unusual new order

explanation.surface: Someone has the right to share out a remarkably plentiful stock of cocoa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges UP COCOA IN, and 'to divide' puts R (right) into the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornucopia is the horn of plenty, so the word stands for any overflowing store.

clue.text: Test a learner after a lot of instruction

indicators.note: after places the a and the learner behind the shortened instruction
a lot of means most but not all of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: an order is an instruction
L is the learner sign on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A pupil is examined after receiving a great deal of teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' drops only the final letter of the instruction word, and 'after' sets the remaining pieces behind it; 'instruction' poses as teaching but means a command.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a severe trial, and historically a trial by fire or water to establish guilt.

clue.text: Politician, hot while in east, is showing stress

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
as can mean while, as in 'as I spoke'

explanation.surface: A politician feeling the heat while out east is under strain.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces fall in the order E, MP, H, AS, IS; 'in' and 'showing' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Stress on a word or point is the weight or importance given to it.

clue.text: Force going south of wood in retreat

indicators.note: in a down clue, going south of means placed below, so after, the wood

parts.note: ash is a kind of wood
to ram is to force, as in ramming something home

explanation.surface: Troops push southwards from a forest as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'going south of' puts RAM below ASH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage, a place of religious seclusion.

clue.text: Supreme officer restrains language, upset about weather conditions

indicators.note: restrains means the officer holds the other piece inside

parts.note: CIC is commander-in-chief, the supreme officer

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the language is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: Tamil is a language of southern India and Sri Lanka

explanation.surface: A top commander curbs a language and gets upset about the weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns the language over and 'restrains' holds it inside the commander; 'about weather conditions' is the whole definition, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Climatic means relating to climate, the long-term pattern of temperature and rainfall.

clue.text: Characters involved in initiation ceremony, formerly

indicators.note: Characters involved in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Letters from an old rite of passage, from times gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters involved in' picks out the letters running from 'initiation' into 'ceremony'.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at some time in the past, the sense of 'once upon a time'.

clue.text: Fly, angry by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word for angry is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: sore can mean angry, especially in American usage

explanation.surface: An insect seems irritated, judging by its buzzing.
explanation.definitionFit: To soar is to rise and glide high in the air.

clue.text: Fine fabric ending in tatters, bitten by rodent, along with rope

indicators.note: bitten by puts the end of tatters into the mouth of the rodent

parts.note: a mouse is a rodent

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of tatters

parts.note: a line is a rope, especially on board ship

explanation.surface: Delicate cloth left in rags after a mouse has chewed it, along with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending in' takes the final S of 'tatters', which 'bitten by' sets inside the rodent; 'along with' just joins on the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousseline is a very fine sheer cloth such as muslin or silk.

clue.text: Disappointing student, say, ultimately sluggish, minded having to turn up in university constantly

indicators.note: in places the turned pieces inside the word for university
to turn up in a down clue reads the pieces upward, so backwards
ultimately picks the final letter of sluggish

parts.note: to have minded is to have cared
ever means constantly, as in 'ever hopeful'

explanation.surface: A lazy student who couldn't care less, forever turning up at college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' reverses the end of 'sluggish' with the word for minded, giving DERACH, which 'in' lodges in the college word; 'say' flags the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil who performs below their ability is the typical example of one who fails to reach potential.

clue.text: Tangled tale's conclusion music magazine dropped

indicators.note: conclusion picks the last letter of tale

parts.note: NME is the New Musical Express, a British music paper
to have shed something is to have dropped it

explanation.surface: The end of the story is that a music magazine was axed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conclusion' gives E from 'tale's'; NME is a long-running British music weekly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something caught as in a net is entangled, held fast by mesh.

clue.text: Glass having unusual value when it's cut

parts.note: rum is an informal word for odd or unusual

indicators.note: cut means the letters named are removed from the word for value

parts.note: merit is value or worth
the it of it's gives the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A drinking glass is oddly worth more once it has been cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the letters of 'it' from the word for value; 'rum' meaning odd is an old British usage, and 'Glass' is a drinking vessel, not a pane.
explanation.definitionFit: A rummer is a large stemmed drinking goblet, once used for toddy.

clue.text: Gather aboard ship for race on river

indicators.note: aboard means the gathering word sits inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS is steamship, the prefix of ship names
to cull is to gather or pick out

explanation.surface: People gather on a vessel to watch a rowing contest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aboard' uses the convention that a word inside SS is on the ship; 'race on river' defines a rowing event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sculls is a rowing contest for single oarsmen with two oars each, like Henley's Diamond Sculls.

clue.text: Least accessible note by doctor connected with experiment

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
MO is a medical officer
a test is an experiment

explanation.surface: A doctor's note relating to a lab trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The most distant place is the hardest to reach.

clue.text: Agreement one in trio sadly wrecked

indicators.note: wrecked signals the letters are smashed up and rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: One member of a trio has unhappily ruined things.
explanation.walkthrough: I (one) plus TRIO and SADLY are rearranged together, as 'wrecked' says; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidarity is unity of purpose among a group, a sense of shared cause.

clue.text: Place filled by a rich cousin corruptly in local administrative body

indicators.note: filled by means the place letters are packed with the rest

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: corruptly says the letters of a rich cousin are twisted into another order

explanation.surface: A wealthy relative dishonestly lands a seat on the local committee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corruptly' rearranges A RICH COUSIN, which fills P...L. A parish council is the lowest tier of English local government.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the elected body running a village or small community in England.

clue.text: Report containing nothing about move

indicators.note: containing means the report word holds the other letters inside

parts.note: to relate is to report or tell
O is the figure zero, nothing
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: An account with nothing about a relocation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' lets the report word swallow the zero and the circa letter; 'move' as a verb is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate is to shift to a new home or site.

clue.text: Outlaw disrupting ceremony led by upper-class resident of city

indicators.note: led by in a down clue puts the upper-class letter at the top

parts.note: U is upper-class, from Nancy Mitford's U and non-U

indicators.note: disrupting means the outlaw word breaks into the ceremony word

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
to ban is to outlaw

explanation.surface: A bandit breaks up a ritual run by a posh town-dweller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupting' breaks the ceremony word open around the ban, and 'led by' puts the posh letter at the top of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An urbanite is a town or metropolis dweller.

clue.text: Good storyteller, one behind account about Mediterranean port

indicators.note: behind places the good storyteller and one after the account
about turns the account letters around

parts.note: G is good
a liar tells stories
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fine raconteur trails behind a story about a southern harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AC to CA; 'storyteller' is a liar who tells untrue stories. Cagliari is the capital of Sardinia.
explanation.definitionFit: Cagliari is the main harbour city of Sardinia, an island in the Med.

clue.text: Top mimic with inward self-esteem rising

indicators.note: with inward means the ego goes inside the mimic word

parts.note: to ape is to mimic

indicators.note: rising in a down clue reads the self-esteem word upwards, so reversed

parts.note: ego is self-esteem

explanation.surface: The best impersonator has growing inner confidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns the self-esteem word upwards in this down entry, and 'with inward' tucks it inside the mimic; 'Top' is a noun, the highest point.
explanation.definitionFit: An apogee is a climax or highest point, originally an orbit's farthest point from Earth.

clue.text: Amount of money needed in past to get a drink

indicators.note: needed in means the money goes inside the past word

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by
the rand is the South African currency

explanation.surface: Some cash was required in former days to buy a tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed in' sets the South African currency inside the word for past, as in 'days gone by'; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Brandy is a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Sign given by man going around river after gold

indicators.note: after places the man and river beneath the gold in this down entry

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: going around means the man word encircles the river letter

parts.note: a guy is a man
R is river

explanation.surface: An omen offered by a fellow wandering the river in search of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going around' wraps the fellow around the river letter, and 'after' puts that below the gold symbol in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An augury is an omen or portent foretelling the future.

clue.text: Plaster almost fixed and firm

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the fixed word is dropped

parts.note: stuck means fixed in place
Co is a company, a firm

explanation.surface: Plaster that has nearly set and is solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' clips the last letter off the word for fixed; 'firm' is the company abbreviation, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine render used to coat walls or make mouldings.

clue.text: One on left wing showing pace

explanation.surface: A left-wing politician setting the speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Trotskyist, informally, is a leftist of a particular stamp; it is also a horse's gait between walk and canter.

clue.text: Sour as a result of change around home, for example

indicators.note: around means the change word surrounds the other letters

parts.note: to vary is to change
in means at home

explanation.surface: Bitterness from upheaval at home, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' has the change word enclose 'at home' plus the abbreviation for 'for example'; 'as a result of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something acidic tastes like spoiled wine.

clue.text: Island with French name recalled by retired sailor with ease

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: nom is French for name

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn backwards, turning the sailor and ease run around

parts.note: a tar is a sailor
rest is ease

explanation.surface: A French-named island remembered by a sailor who has taken to a life of leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns NOM to MON; 'retired' turns TAR plus REST into TSERRAT. Montserrat is a British territory in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Montserrat is a volcanic Caribbean territory in the Leeward chain.

clue.text: Judge furious when one's released

indicators.note: released means the one is let go, taken out of the furious word

parts.note: irate means furious
one gives the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A judge, livid when a prisoner is freed.
explanation.walkthrough: IRATE loses I, as 'released' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to assess or evaluate it.
